Revival of Romanticism took place in the Romantic Period. Lyrical Ballads brought about a great change in literature, both in subject and style.

English-03.question: ৩) The duration of ‘Jacobean Period’ of English Literature is -
English-03.exp:
The Renaissance Period of English Literature (1500-1660) has four parts:
1. Elizabethan Age (1558 - 1603)
2. Jacobean Age (1603 - 1625)
3. Caroline Age (1625 - 1649)
4. Commonwealth Age (1649 -1660)
Main literary feature of the Jacobean Period:
1) Renaissance spirit remains
2) Elizabethan verse disappears
3) Masque is innovated
4) Satiric art begins
5) English language develops further
Source: Live MCQ Lecture and An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

Thomas Kyd, John Lyly, Robert Greene, George Peele, Christopher Marlowe and Thomas Nashe are university wits.

English-03.question: ১৬) What type of literary work 'The Taming of the Shrew' is?
English-03.exp:
The Taming of the Shrew is a comedy in five acts by William Shakespeare, written sometime in 1590–94 and first printed in the First Folio of 1623.
The play describes the volatile courtship between the shrewish Katharina (Kate) and the canny Petruchio, who is determined to subdue Katharina’s legendary temper and win her dowry.

The main story is offered as a play within a play; the frame plot consists of an initial two-scene “induction” in which a whimsical lord decides to play a practical joke on a drunken tinker, Christopher Sly, by inducing him to believe that he is in fact a nobleman who has suffered from amnesia and is only now awaking from it.

Source: Britannica.com

English-03.question:
৩৪) ''To Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love
All pray in their distress''
These lines are taken from-
English-03.exp:
To Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love
All pray in their distress;
And to these virtues of delight
Return their thankfulness.

For Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love
Is God, our father dear,
And Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love
Is Man, his child and care.

-The Divine Image
By - WILLIAM BLAKE

The Divine Image is part of Songs of Innocence.
Songs of Innocence was first published in 1789 followed by the publication of Songs of Experience in 1794. William Blake mostly wrote romantic poetry and prophetic works.
The Divine Image portrays an ideal world. The poem presents four traditional Christian virtues (Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love), which exist in the human heart and connect it with God.

The first version, published in 1712, consisted of two cantos; the final version, published in 1714, was expanded to five cantos.
